advisory_notes: The supplied extract is truncated and does not substantiate the title or release date; web evidence shows publication on 14 November 2026 and supports substantive export figures [1].
The note’s statement that the record contains only a title is contradicted by the accessible release, which reports April–October totals, merchandise and services exports, and growth rates [1][2].
The background mechanism is sound analysis, but distinguish it from source-reported evidence rather than implying that the release itself establishes it.

The GS3.1 and GS3.4 mapping is broadly relevant to growth, development, employment, inclusive growth and external-sector issues, though the exact code labels are coaching-framework labels rather than official UPSC numbering [5][6].

The proposed use line appropriately cautions against inferring institutional or numerical claims, but it should be updated because the release does provide several numbers and policy-context claims [1].
The export-led-growth definition and policy recommendations are analytical framing, not independently evidenced facts; label them as conceptual analysis.
The claim that the release does not identify any policy measures is too categorical: the accessible release refers to export-promotion measures, trade partnerships and logistics improvements [1].

wayForward: Build competitiveness through reliable logistics, quality infrastructure, technology adoption and predictable trade procedures.

Evaluate export policy through employment, regional inclusion, environmental sustainability, resilience and the trade balance, not only gross export value.
